transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I guess... well, I've just been having a little trouble at work lately. I'm an orderly, you know, and I try really hard to do a good job, but... 

It's just that my words get a little jumbled sometimes. Like, I'll be trying to tell a nurse about something from my overnight shift, and then somehow I'm talking about soccer, or the color of the paint on the walls, and then back to patient charts. It's probably just me being tired, right? But I can tell people are getting a little confused when I talk. I just want to make sure I'm making sense. Am I making sense right now?
Besides the trouble organizing your words, have you noticed any changes in your mood lately—like feeling unusually elated, energetic, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Oh, um, no. No, Dr. Smith. I haven't really felt like that at all. Not elated or... or full of energy. Honestly, I'm usually just pretty tired. I try really hard to get my sleep so I can be ready for my shifts, you know? I want to be reliable for the nurses. 

So I definitely haven't been staying awake or feeling wired. I hope that's okay? I mean, I hope it's okay that I don't have that going on. I'm just trying to give you the right answers, I promise. But no, no extra energy or anything like that.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people didn't seem to notice, or had strong beliefs that others thought were unusual or untrue?

Um... voices? No, no, I don't hear anything like that. I promise. I'm really normal that way. But, um... you asked about things other people think aren't true? 

I... I hope you won't think I'm a bad employee or anything for saying this, because I really try so hard to do a good job. But... I'm sure the supervisors have been changing my shifts on purpose. And... well, I know they watch me through the unit cameras. I think they're trying to see if I'm unsafe on the floor. I'm not, I swear! I'm really careful and gentle with the patients. But they keep watching me on the monitors. 

When I brought it up, people just told me it's only staffing shortages causing all the schedule changes, but... I just know they're watching me. Does that make sense? I hope it doesn't make me sound, you know, paranoid or difficult to work with. I really am a good orderly, I promise.
How long have you been noticing these thoughts about being watched and the trouble organizing your words—has this been going on for weeks, or longer, like several months?

Um, well... I guess it's been a little while. I mean, not forever! Just... maybe around a year? Or a year and a month, something like that? 

I hope that doesn't sound too bad. I really tried to just put my head down and work hard, you know? I didn't want to complain or make a fuss about the cameras or my words getting mixed up. I figured if I just kept being a good orderly, it wouldn't matter. It's not like it happens every single second of the day. 

Is it... is it bad that it's been going on that long? I should have said something sooner, shouldn't I? I'm sorry, I just really didn't want to cause any trouble for the nurses or the supervisors.
Have you had any recent head injuries, seizures, significant medical illnesses, or been using any drugs, alcohol, or new medications around the time these thoughts and speech changes started?

Um, no, Dr. Smith. Nothing like that. I don't drink, and I definitely don't do any drugs. I know how important it is to be clear-headed for the patients, so I would never do anything to jeopardize that. I don't even take any new medications, just some ibuprofen if my back hurts from lifting, but that's it.

And I haven't hit my head or been sick or anything. I've been perfectly healthy, physically anyway. I really try to take good care of myself so I don't have to call out sick. I hope that's the right answer? I mean, I'm just telling the truth, but I hope it helps you figure things out. I really am trying to be a good patient for you.
Have you noticed any recent problems with your memory, concentration, or feeling confused about where you are or what day it is?

Um, no, I definitely know where I am and what day it is! I'm always on time for work, I promise. I would never let the unit down by forgetting a shift or anything like that. 

But, um... as for concentration... I feel a little bad admitting this, because I really pride myself on being sharp for the nurses and the patients. But lately, I guess... well, sometimes I can read the exact same page of a patient note, or even just one of my own bills at home, like three times, and I still just don't know what it says. It's like the words are there but my brain just kind of blanks on them. And even with really little things, like trying to pick what to buy at the grocery store... it can just completely freeze me up. 

I hope you don't think I'm incompetent or anything because of that. I always make sure to double-check everything I do at work so everyone stays safe, I swear. Do you think that's just from stress? I really hope I'm answering all these questions okay for you.
Have you noticed changes in how you're doing with things outside of work, like maintaining friendships, taking care of things at home, or your usual daily routines?

Um, well... I guess things have been a little tough outside of work, too. I mean, I really try to keep everything together, I promise. But... well, my apartment is a bit messy right now. Not, like, a disaster! Just... out of control, I guess. And I haven't really been keeping up with my bills like I usually do. I know that sounds irresponsible, and I'm really sorry, I'm usually so much better about that stuff. 

And, um, my friends... I've kind of been ignoring them. I just haven't had the energy, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad friend. 

Even at work, I... well, I've had to ask some of my coworkers to double-check my rounds and my charting. Just to be safe! I didn't want to make any mistakes with the patients. But I guess it was a lot, because... well, employee health actually sent me here for an emergency evaluation. 

I really didn't want to tell you this part, because I don't want you to think I'm crazy or dangerous, but... I told them I was having some thoughts about, um, suicide. I'm so sorry, I know that's probably really alarming to hear. I just... things got really overwhelming. I hope you're not mad at me for letting it get that bad before getting help. I really am trying to do the right thing now.

Aside from the recent low mood and low energy, has there been a time—maybe earlier in the year—when you were feeling okay emotionally, not depressed, but still noticed the jumbled speech or the feeling that you were being watched?

Um, well... I guess, yeah. There was a time, maybe a few months ago? I wasn't feeling so down and heavy like I am now. I actually felt okay, emotionally, I mean. I was getting out of bed fine and everything. 

But... well, I still felt like I was being watched. I was still really sure about the cameras, and that the supervisors were monitoring everything I did on the unit. I was being really careful and, I guess, guarded at work during that time, even though I wasn't depressed. 

I hope that makes sense? I know it probably sounds strange that I was still acting like that when my mood was fine. I'm really trying to give you the whole picture so you can help me. Does that help answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Over this past year, would you say the low mood and low energy have been present most of the time, or has it mainly been these last few weeks/months, with many months before that where you felt emotionally fine despite still feeling watched?

Um... well, I guess if I really look back at the whole year... I mean, I want to say I was fine most of the time, because I really try to be positive, you know? But... if I'm being completely honest, that heavy, empty feeling... and just not caring about things I used to like... it's kind of been there for most of the year. 

Even when the worries about the cameras weren't so bad, or when my thoughts weren't getting all jumbled up... that low mood was still just kind of hanging over me. I know I said earlier I felt okay for a little bit, and I did, I swear! I just... I guess overall, the sadness has been there a lot more than I wanted to admit. 

I'm sorry if that's confusing, changing my answer a little bit like that. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate timeline so you can do your job. Is that what you needed to know? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough.

Thinking back to that stretch of a few months ago when you said your mood felt okay—can you tell me roughly how many weeks in a row you felt emotionally fine while still having those thoughts about being watched?

Um... let me think. I really want to give you the exact right answer. I guess... it was probably just a stretch of a few weeks? Yeah, maybe like three or four weeks where I wasn't in that really deep, heavy depressed place. I was actually waking up okay and everything. 

But... um... I still completely believed the cameras were there, and that the supervisors were monitoring everything I did. So I kept acting really guarded at work during those weeks, just to be safe. I know it's probably disappointing to hear that I was still having those thoughts even when my mood was better... I'm sorry, I really was trying my best to just be normal. 

Does that help? Is a few weeks the kind of timeline you were looking for?

Doctor: Okay, thank you for clarifying that timeline. Now, have you ever experienced a period where your mood was the opposite of depressed—where you felt extremely energetic, needed very little sleep, had racing thoughts, or felt unusually confident or "high" for several days in a row?

Patient: Oh, um... no. No, I haven't ever felt like that. I mean, I know sometimes people get really energetic and, you know, kind of out of control, but I've never been like that. I've always just been... well, mostly just dealing with the low mood and the worries about work. 

I've never had a time where I didn't need sleep or felt super confident. I'm usually pretty quiet and just try to do my job. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm not supposed to have felt that way for you to figure out what's wrong with me. But no, I haven't had any of those high energy times. Is that what you needed to know?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient demonstrates persistent psychotic symptoms (paranoid delusions about surveillance, disorganized/tangential speech) lasting about one year, meeting Criterion A for schizophrenia-spectrum illness. Concurrently, she reports a major depressive syndrome (depressed mood, anhedonia, poor concentration, psychomotor/functional decline, suicidal ideation) present for the majority of the illness duration. Critically, she also identifies a distinct 3-4 week period during which psychotic symptoms (delusions of being watched) persisted in the absence of significant mood disturbance, satisfying the requirement for delusions/hallucinations for ≥2 weeks without a major mood episode. No manic/hypomanic symptoms were ever endorsed. This combination—mood episode overlapping with psychosis for the majority of the illness course, plus a discrete period of psychosis without mood symptoms, plus mood symptoms present for the majority of total illness duration—is diagnostic of Schizoaffective Disorder, Depressive Type (F25.1), rather than Schizophrenia (which would require mood symptoms to be brief/minor) or Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features (which would require psychosis to occur only during mood episodes).
